sections.html:
Central Arkansas is home to Faulkner County, where Conway serves as both seat and biggest city. The 2020 population was 123,498, fifth highest among Arkansas counties. Interstate 40 made Conway and the towns around it commuter communities for Little Rock, and that steady demand is part of what shapes house prices here.

Mayflower, Vilonia, Greenbrier, Guy, Holland, Enola, Mount Vernon, Quitman, Wooster and Damascus are separate towns. Greenbrier and Vilonia have their own schools and city rules. Before you compare bills with a neighbor, check which school district and city appear on yours.

Two county offices shape your bill. One sets the value and the other sends the statement and takes the money. The Assessor is at 806 Faulkner Street in Conway, phone 501-450-4905, with a second location at 89 N Broadview Street in Greenbrier. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 4:30 p.m.

The Collector's phone is 501-450-4921. Conway keeps the same weekday schedule. The Greenbrier office at 89 N Broadview Street opens earlier on Monday through Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and closes at noon on Friday after opening at 8:00 a.m.

  • Mail, in-person and online payments are all taken.
  • Online payments go through actdatascout.com/faulknerar, and a card fee applies.
  • Pay personal property tax first or together with real estate tax. An electronic real estate payment is refused until the personal property bill is cleared.
  • Statements are mailed in spring. If nothing has arrived by July 1, phone the Collector.

Taxes here run one year behind, so what you pay now covers the prior year's assessment. The collection season starts March 1 and closes October 15, and a weekend or holiday on the last day pushes it to the next business day.

Anything paid after October 15 draws a 10 percent penalty on both real estate and personal property. Late real estate tax carries 10 percent annual interest on top.

ObligationWhen it runsCost of being late
Pay real estate taxMarch 1 through October 1510 percent penalty, plus 10 percent annual interest
Assess personal propertyFirst working day of January through May 3110 percent late assessment fee
Assess a newly bought itemWithin 30 days of buyingLate assessment fee applies

The Assessor expects the current reappraisal cycle to wrap up in 2028. Arkansas counties reappraise every 3, 4 or 5 years. Asking which year crews last covered your neighborhood tells you when your value is likely to move.

Appraisers generally stay outside. Interior rooms are not inspected and measurements are approximate, so read your property record for wrong square footage or missing features.

Call the Assessor first, since a plain data mistake may be corrected with no hearing at all. Still unhappy? Request a hearing before the County Board of Equalization. Its five members equalize assessed values under Arkansas Code 26-27-301 through 26-27-325, and the third Monday in August is the last day to get on the schedule. Take photos of defects, repair estimates and recent sales of comparable houses nearby.

If you live in the house, you can claim a homestead credit worth up to $600 a year. The application for the current tax bill is due October 15. Check your bill, or call the Collector, for the exact amount.

Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, may qualify for a freeze on the taxable value of a principal residence. Both benefits follow the person living there. A buyer has to reapply after moving in, so neither transfers with the deed, and the first bill the buyer sees can run higher than yours.

The April 27, 2014 tornado, rated EF4, destroyed or heavily damaged homes in Mayflower and Vilonia, including the Parkwood Meadows subdivision in Vilonia and the River Plantation subdivision in Mayflower. Twelve of its 16 deaths were in Faulkner County. Homes along Lake Conway were also damaged.

Buyers in these areas ask about past storms, and a clear answer helps a sale move along.

  • Say whether the roof, slab or storm shelter was rebuilt after a past storm.
  • Keep permit records for repairs.
  • Photograph damage you did not repair, since buyers will ask.

sections.h2: If your house has storm repairs or unpermitted work
sections.html:
Open-ended questions slow a sale more than the repairs themselves. If a contractor fixed the roof after hail or wind, find the invoice. If you added a deck, carport or storage building, look for the permit. A missing permit does not end a sale, but telling a buyer early lets them price it in rather than discover it during an inspection.

A buyer paying cash can take the house as it stands and adjust the price for what needs work. A buyer with a lender usually cannot, because an appraisal and inspection feed the loan decision. That difference is the main reason owners of storm-worn or heavily used houses look at direct sales.

Deeds are recorded by the Circuit Clerk, who acts as ex-officio recorder, at 724 Locust Avenue in Conway, phone 501-450-4911. Budget $15 for page one of a deed and $5 for each page after that, while a plat or survey runs $15.

Land records are online, and the clerk lists e-recording vendors that title companies use to file without a trip to the courthouse. You can also sign up for a free email alert that fires when a document is indexed under your name. Arkansas also taxes the transfer at $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration. Records can be searched at ARCountyData.com and ActDataScout.com, which the Assessor says update monthly.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
A few documents save time once an offer arrives. Pull your last tax statement and the receipt showing it was paid. Find the deed, any survey or plat, and permit paperwork for roof, slab or storm shelter work. If you claimed the homestead credit or the senior freeze, note that the new owner starts fresh.

Call the Assessor to confirm the parcel number and acreage on file, and ask the clerk whether any older instruments are indexed against the property. Cleaning up a mismatch before a buyer finds it keeps the timeline short and avoids a last-minute delay at the title company.

Sellers who live outside the county, such as heirs, can handle most of this by phone and email. Because records are searchable from home, an heir in another state seldom needs to visit Conway in person.

After you accept an offer, the title company opens an order and runs a search on the property. The search turns up unpaid taxes, liens and any recorded problems. You then receive a settlement statement listing the tax payoff, recording fees and the transfer tax.

On closing day you sign the deed. The title company records it with the Circuit Clerk and pays off the tax balance from proceeds. With a cash buyer and a clean title search, this can finish on a date you choose rather than on a lender's schedule.

Because the county bills a year behind, a closing often lands while some tax is still owed. Get the parcel's balance from the Collector, with any penalty and interest included, and hand it to the title company. The balance comes out of your sale proceeds, and the settlement statement shows how the year's bill is split with the buyer.

If you owe personal property tax, settle it first. An unpaid personal property balance blocks the electronic real estate payment, and that can slow the payoff.

A cash sale skips showings, appraisals and repair requests. The tax payoff and the recording steps do not change. Set any written offer next to your payoff figure to see what you would walk away with.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my Faulkner County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Collector takes payment at the Conway courthouse office, at the Greenbrier branch, through the mail and online. Call 501-450-4921 with questions.

faqs.q: How much is the late charge in Faulkner County?
faqs.a: Ten percent, applied after October 15. Real estate tax also accrues 10 percent annual interest.

faqs.q: Can I pay Faulkner County real estate tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, through actdatascout.com/faulknerar with a card fee. Personal property tax has to be paid first, because real estate cannot be paid electronically until it is.

faqs.q: When will Faulkner County finish its current reappraisal?
faqs.a: The Assessor says 2028. Ask which year your neighborhood was last visited.

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my homestead credit?
faqs.a: No. The new owner files a fresh application after moving in.
